rationale: Archive and exclude the published TransAlta Keephills Data Centre JV row because direct sources support only an early-stage proposed Keephills data-centre development under a conditional memorandum of understanding. No separate JV or SPV, CPP Investments equity stake, investment vehicle, definitive joint-venture agreement, committed capital, PPA or lease, financial close or legal investment close was verified. Remove the erroneous active CPP ownership period and do not create a pending ownership transaction; retain the project record only as archived evidence of the monitored proposal.

supports: TransAlta continued to describe the arrangement as a conditional MOU
No definitive equity closing was disclosed through the latest filing
The project remained subject to future definitive binding agreements
TransAlta was the exclusive site and power provider
The MOU did not mean a data centre was being built
The proposal remained in early planning

beforeImage.name: TransAlta Keephills Data Centre JV
beforeImage.description: TransAlta Keephills Data Centre JV is a development partnership for a large Alberta data-center project linked to dedicated power supply at the Keephills site. The venture is designed to serve high-density computing demand and depends on both digital-infrastructure development and long-term power procurement. Its model is asset-heavy because value is tied to site control, major capital deployment, and integrated electricity infrastructure rather than an asset-light colocation strategy. TransAlta announced in 2026 that it had entered into an MOU with CPP Investments and Brookfield for an initial approximately 230 MW project with potential to scale to 1 GW. Public sources reviewed do not disclose the ownership percentages of the development partners.

milestones.event: The partners disclosed an initial approximately 230 MW project supported by a long-term power arrangement.
The project had the potential to scale to as much as 1 GW over time.
The development advanced as a powered data-center opportunity in Alberta.
TransAlta Keephills Data Centre JV was founded.
TransAlta announced an MOU with CPP Investments and Brookfield for data-center development at its Keephills site.

afterImage.name: TransAlta Keephills Data Centre JV
afterImage.description: Archived proposed data-centre development at TransAlta's Keephills site in Parkland County, Alberta. TransAlta signed a memorandum of understanding on February 26, 2026 with CPP Investments and Brookfield as prospective proponents or customers for an initial approximately 230 MW phase with potential to scale to 1 GW. Direct sources state that the proposal remained subject to regulatory approvals and future definitive binding agreements; no separate JV or SPV, CPP equity stake, investment vehicle, committed capital, definitive joint-venture agreement, PPA or lease, financial close or legal investment close was verified through August 19, 2026. AESO grid-connection activity is project-development evidence, not manager ownership. The row is therefore excluded from the active PortCo census and carries no ownership period or pending ownership transaction; it may be reassessed only after a verifiable definitive equity agreement and close.

milestones.event: AESO recorded the application date for the initial Keephills Phase 1 load project; this was a grid-connection milestone, not a CPP Investments equity entry.
TransAlta signed a conditional memorandum of understanding with CPP Investments and Brookfield for the proposed Keephills development.
TransAlta announced an initial approximately 230 MW concept with potential to scale to 1 GW, subject to regulatory approvals and future definitive agreements.
TransAlta's second-quarter filing continued to describe the arrangement as an MOU subject to definitive agreements, with no investment close disclosed.
AESO listed the phased Keephills load projects in grid-connection review or active processing; those entries did not identify a CPP investment vehicle or ownership stake.
